page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSv2 family. It features 208 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 104 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 5700.0 GB, providing approximately 27.4 GB of RAM per core, and includes 8389 GB of local storage with support for Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data highlights a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and single-threaded decompression, rank in the bottom 25%, the massive core count drives multi-core performance into the top 10% tier. This is evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 187,922.32 and a Passmark CPU score of 86,616.03. Memory bandwidth is also highly performant, reaching top-tier status with read-only small block cached speeds of 10,446.46 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds of 347.19 GB/sec. Additionally, the instance achieved a top-tier Redis SET operations throughput of 162.62 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a high-density, premium hardware class designed for workloads where massive memory capacity is non-negotiable. The primary tradeoff is the relatively weak single-threaded execution speed, meaning it is poorly suited for sequential, non-parallelized tasks. However, its massive RAM-to-vCPU ratio and exceptional multi-threaded capabilities make it highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, heavy multi-threaded data processing, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, featuring 208 dedicated vCPUs across 104 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores at 2.7 GHz. It is equipped with 5700.0 GB of RAM and 8389 GB of local storage, with no integrated GPUs. While single-core benchmarks are relatively weak, the instance delivers top-tier multi-core and memory performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 187,922.32 and a Redis throughput of 162.62 million operations per second. It is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise database systems, and highly parallelized data processing workloads.
